front.label: Front addition
front.title: A modern warm-white front.
front.text: Smooth warm-white stucco wraps the front walls, gables, bay base and corner returns, under a charcoal standing-seam roof with charcoal fascia. Slim matte-black frames hold large clear panes. Warm vertical wood cladding lines the recessed entry around the walnut front door, and a stained-cedar carriage-house garage door with a top row of glass lites, flanked by black coach lanterns, completes the front. Bedroom 3 keeps its tall bay window and a solid gable above it. The rectangular high window over the entrance, the vaulted front bedroom and the coordinated rooflines are retained. Roof forms are inferred from your aerial photo; dimensions remain proposed.

B3.label: Bedroom 3
B3.title: A canted bay glazed to the floor.
B3.text: Slim black frames with large clear panes run from the floor to the 7′6″ head, so the bay reads as part of the room and opens it to the front garden. The floor extends into the bay. The bed sits on the west wall to keep it open. Bay: 8′ wall opening, 2′ projection, glazed to the floor. Above the bay is a continuous plaster gable, and the vaulted ceiling rises to 11′6″ at the ridge, lit by a ring pendant. The bathroom and compact closet remain on the opposite wall, with the hall entrance at the side. The foyer wall lines up with the shared bathroom's wall, so the room is 14′10⅜″ wide.

B4.label: Bedroom 4
B4.title: Bedroom 4: a flat ceiling and the bed turned across the room.
B4.text: A calm flat ceiling replaces the vault, at the same 8 ft as the rest of the house. The full bed is turned across the room, with its headboard on the north wall and its side along the window wall, so the room's length stays open from the bed to the door and the reach-in closet. The desk stands in a niche on the north wall, between the nightstand and the back wall of the laundry closet, which takes the room's north-east corner and opens onto the foyer. The room (the architect's office), its separate reach-in closet and the west-facing window keep their positions; overall the room is still 8′0″ deep as on the architect's plan and 14′10⅜″ wide, because its foyer wall lines up with the shared bathroom's wall, and it is now L-shaped around the laundry closet.

K0.label: Kitchen
K0.title: A warm vintage kitchen in cream, oak and brass.
K0.text: Cream shaker cabinets with unlacquered brass cup pulls and knobs, glass-front uppers and a greige pantry wall with a panelled fridge and stainless wall ovens. A cream plaster hood with a dentil band rises over a scalloped marble backsplash and a brass pot filler, beside walnut open shelves on whitewashed brick. The fireclay farmhouse sink sits under the black grid window with brass sconces and linen café curtains. Amber-glass pendants hang over a white-oak island with a thick grey-veined quartzite top and a Persian runner, and a warm oak dining table for six continues the island's west end, toward the hall, under a brass lantern, so the floor between the island and the family room stays open. A 3′6″ × 4′ skylight sits on the continuous east roof plane, over the sink and dishwasher. Proposed window: 6′ wide, 3′1¾″ sill, 7′9″ head. Styled after your kitchen style images.

A0.label: Primary bathroom
A0.title: Sage tile, solid oak and stone in the primary bath.
A0.text: A glossy sage-green subway-tiled shower sits behind frameless glass with an aged-brass rain shower and hand shower, under the 2′0″ × 2′6″ skylight. A floating solid-oak slab with two basins carved into the wood hangs under brass-framed mirrors and brass sconces, against sage V-groove panelling with warm cream plaster above. A stacked-stone wall frames the wall-hung toilet and a reclaimed-timber shelf, and the floor is blue-and-cream encaustic tile. The tall clear window between the vanity and the shower now starts at a 2′0″ sill, with a linen roman shade. Styled after your primary bathroom style images.

A1.label: Shared bathroom
A1.title: A wood-look wall and warm stone in the shared bath.
A1.text: A rustic oak wood-look tile wall rises behind the wall-hung toilet and around a softly lit, wood-lined niche, with warm Spanish-cream stone-look porcelain on the other walls. A floating light-oak vanity carries a honed travertine block with a carved trough basin, a wall-mounted brushed-nickel faucet and a backlit mirror. The floor is light limestone-look tile, and the alcove tub keeps its glass screen and lit niche. The existing tub, vanity, toilet orientation and room footprint remain. Styled after your shared bathroom style images.

roof.label: Roof connections
roof.title: Roof planes meet at defined ridges and sloped valleys.
roof.text: The broad main hip and front garage gable follow the forms visible in IMG_3202.PNG. The new 6:12 bedroom gable continues over Bedrooms 3 and 4. A small drainage cricket at the rear hip connection removes a level trough and directs water into sloped valleys. A lower entry gable has a slight fall toward the front so the side valleys are not level. The entry clerestory is coordinated to 3′ × 2′3″. Main and garage 4:12 pitches are provisional. The roof is shown in charcoal standing-seam metal. This is a concept roof model; field measurements, framing and drainage detailing remain to be resolved.

LC.label: Laundry closet
LC.title: A stacked washer and dryer off the foyer, next to Bedroom 4.
LC.text: The laundry closet is carved out of Bedroom 4's north-east corner and opens onto the foyer, on its west side right next to the bedroom door. A front-load washer with the dryer stacked on top stands centred behind a pair of narrow doors in a 2′6″ × 6′8″ opening; the doors are hinged on the two jambs and shown wide open against the foyer wall. The closet is 2′10″ wide and 3′0″ deep inside, under the 8 ft ceiling; the oak floor runs in from the foyer, a recessed outlet box and the dryer vent are on the back wall, and a flush light sits in the ceiling. Bedroom 4 keeps its overall size and is L-shaped around the closet. The units are generic models of a typical stacked pair (27″ wide, 30¼″ deep, 39″ high each), not a selected product: connections, vent route and clearances need to be confirmed for the appliances you choose.

changes: Bedroom 4 (plan: office): flat 8 ft ceiling instead of the vault
Front bedroom bay (tour: Bedroom 3, plan: Bedroom #2): glazed down to the floor; window seat removed
Foyer: two skylights on the entry roof's east slope (hall section and vaulted entry)
Primary bedroom: the 7 ft rear window becomes a two-panel sliding door to the garden (landing outside)
Bedroom 2 (next to the primary): rear window runs to the ceiling (sill 2'-0" since the third round)
Primary bathroom: tall west window in clear glass, between vanity and shower, sill 2'-0" since the third round (an evergreen screen in the fenced side yard outside)
Kitchen skylight: 3'-6" x 4'-0" on the continuous east roof plane over the sink / dishwasher (the concept unit straddled the garage-gable ridge)
Dining: table in line with the island, no island stools (warm oak under a brass lantern since the third round; moved to the island's west end, 6'-0" x 2'-9" for six, in the fifth round)
Primary bathroom: a 2'-0" x 2'-6" skylight over the shower

The foyer-side wall of Bedroom 4 (office) and Bedroom 3 lines up with the shared bath's east wall: both rooms and the closets between them are 1'-2 3/4" wider; foyer and covered porch 5'-9 1/4" wide; foyer 18'-6" long as on the plan; the 3'-0" front door stays centred
Rear landing outside the living room sized as on the plan (3'-0" deep, garden door to x 38'-3")
Bedroom 2 rear window and the primary bathroom window: a 2'-0" sill instead of glass to the floor (heads stay at the 8 ft ceiling)
Bedroom 4: the bed is turned across the room, headboard on the north wall, so the room's length stays open
Kitchen, primary bathroom, shared bathroom and garage door restyled from the owner's style images (styles/)

Laundry closet with a stacked front-load washer and dryer behind a 2'-6" x 6'-8" door opening. It was first built in the kitchen's south-west corner, where the architect's sheet SKA002 draws "W / D": superseded by the fifth round, which moves it to Bedroom 4
Kitchen south wall re-planned around that closet (closet, refrigerator, wall ovens, a short counter, the cooktop): superseded by the fifth round, the wall is back to its third-round layout

Laundry closet moved out of the kitchen: it is carved out of Bedroom 4's north-east corner and opens east onto the foyer, on the foyer's west side next to the bedroom door. 2'-10" wide x 3'-0" deep clear, the stacked front-load washer and dryer behind a pair of doors in a 2'-6" x 6'-8" opening, shown open

Bedroom 4 is L-shaped after the cut: 14'-10 3/8" x 8'-0" overall as before, less 3'-4 3/8" x 3'-2 1/4" for the closet and its two walls (108.2 sq ft); the desk stands in the niche between the nightstand and the closet's back wall

Dining table moved from the family-room side of the island to the island's west end, the shared-bathroom side, in line with the island: 6'-0" x 2'-9", three chairs on each long side, none at the ends, no rug; the floor between the island and the family room is open
Kitchen south wall back to its third-round layout: refrigerator and double ovens at the west (hall) end, then the counter under three glass-front uppers and the cooktop under the hood
